note: THE SECOND OPINION. Every other statement in this estate about what commodity a product is descends from the include regex in commodities.json - so every downstream check inherits that one premise. This file records what the STORE ITSELF says a product is, taken from the store's own feed, and names the departments the store uses for non-edible goods. It is DATA, not a rule library: the department names are quoted verbatim from the store's own taxonomy, never invented. audit-store-taxonomy.ps1 reads it.
rule: A department that appears in a store's feed but is listed in NEITHER food_departments NOR nonfood_departments is reported as UNKNOWN and its rows are NOT judged. Never add a department here without reading the store's own products in it - guessing turns this file back into the 40:1 rule library it exists to replace.

Family Fare.vocabulary_source: 3492 of 3671 rows in out\regular\family-fare-regular-2026-07-30.json carried canonical_url; the 13 department names below are the complete observed vocabulary

commodity_department_allow.reason: Family Fare shelves protein/meal bars in health_beauty/adult_nutrition, so the whole protein-bars commodity legitimately lives in a non-food department. Measured 2026-07-30: without this entry the audit flags 34 candidate rows of which 17 are correct products; with it, 17 flags and 17 were adjudicated wrong by hand. This is the ONLY commodity in the 2870-row Family Fare sample that legitimately sits in a non-food department.
